samples.summary: `renderCoderabbitLatency` re-implements the adapter's exported `latencyAbsentLine` formatter instead of reusing it
`coderabbitLatency` computes `latencyCensus(perItem)` twice and emits `triggers` as a duplicate of `census.triggers`
samples.evidence: `triggers: latencyCensus(perItem).triggers` (line ~651) and `census: latencyCensus(perItem)` (line ~656) call the adapter census twice on the same input, and the resulting payload carries the same trigger tally under two keys (`coderabbit.latency.triggers` and `coderabbit.latency.census.triggers`). One fact in two places in the emitted schema is the exact drift hazard this file's own docblocks argue against elsewhere ("putting it on 30 records would be 30 places for one fact to drift", coderabbit.mjs:1147-1149); a consumer that reads one and a report line that reads the other cannot be shown to agree. One call, and either a single key or an explicit alias, would say the same thing.

samples.summary: The retained `coderabbit_latency_ms` gap loses the interval name and the measured rejected mechanisms the canonical doc says the gap carries
samples.evidence: The gap's `reason` is now the shared `LATENCY_NOT_REQUESTED` string, which names only the flag and the offline-reproducibility rule. The prior reason deliberately carried three things: the decided interval name (`coderabbit-start-marker-to-first-finding`), the rejected mechanisms *with their measured errors* (the status comment's `created_at→updated_at` pair, wrong by 8x; the push proxy that times a human; PR `created_at`/committer date), and the non-comparability note. docs/tasks/active/20260812-eval-cost-latency-scorer-todo.md:270-273 states the gap "is rewritten rather than deleted, and it now carries three things it did not: the interval's name, the rejected mechanisms *with* their measured errors, and the fact that arriving at a number does not make the two arms comparable" — only the third survives (in `unblocked_by`), and the tests asserting the first two were deleted (cost-latency.test.mjs, the `/created_at-to-updated_at pair, which is wrong by 8x/` and `/coderabbit-start-marker-to-first-finding/` assertions). The history now lives only in the adapter's docblocks, and the same doc's stated rule is that "a deleted wrong answer gets reinvented". Either the reason should keep the interval name plus a pointer to the rejected mechanisms, or the follow-up section should record that this was intentionally relocated to the adapter.

samples.summary: `scripts/agent/eval/README.md` is not updated: it still says the cost/latency scorer is unbuilt and that the remaining scorers read "through `EvalStore` and nothing else", which this change falsifies
samples.evidence: README.md:30-32 reads "The cross-arm matcher and the remaining scorers — complementarity, reliability, cost and latency — are not built yet. When they arrive they read items through `EvalStore` and nothing else." The module table also carries an explicit network column (`no (reads gh)` on `adapters/coderabbit.mjs`). This diff gives `cost-latency.mjs`'s CLI a `gh`-backed read via `corpusRecords`, so the directory's own index now states the opposite of what the code does for the one property the table exists to track. The staleness about "not built yet" is pre-existing, but the network claim becomes wrong because of this change and nothing in the diff touches the README.
searchedFor: Read docs/tasks/active/20260812-eval-cost-latency-scorer-todo.md (follow-up section is appended to the canonical doc — that part is fine)

samples.summary: The CLI reaches the other arm through `corpusRecords`, fetching commits/comments/reviews per item only to discard the records
samples.evidence: `corpusRecords(store, corpusVersion).map((it) => ({ item_id, latency }))` runs `fetchCodeRabbitPr` per item — commits, review comments, reviews, issue comments and check runs — and `codeRabbitRecords` on top, then throws all but `latency` away. The discard is deliberate and correct per the non-goal ("No finding counts"), but it means the timing read costs roughly 5 API calls per item where 2 would do, and it couples this scorer to the record-derivation path it does not use. A latency-only entry point in the adapter (`latencyRecords`, reusing `latencyOf`) would keep the ownership split intact at lower cost; not blocking, and correctly left to the module that owns the read.

samples.summary: Module header still frames the file as needing "no second arm" and closes with an unqualified "reads a store, computes, prints", now that the CLI has an opt-in network read
samples.evidence: Lines 4-5 ("the only one in Wave 3 that needs no labels, no matcher and no second arm to be computable") and line 50 ("NOTHING IS WRITTEN AND NOTHING IS SPENT. It reads a store, computes, prints.") are the header a reader trusts before reading the CLI. The USAGE block and the `main()` comment do state that `--coderabbit-latency` makes `gh api` calls, but the header — which the rest of the file uses to declare its boundaries — does not mention that the file now has a network path at all. One clause in the header would keep the file's own summary of itself accurate.

finding.summary: `renderCoderabbitLatency` re-implements the adapter's exported `latencyAbsentLine` formatter instead of reusing it

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. `scripts/agent/eval/cost-latency.mjs:990-995` builds the absence census line inline: `const declared = LATENCY_ABSENT.map((f) => `${f}=${absent[f] ?? 0}`)` and `const extra = Object.keys(absent).filter((f) => !LATENCY_ABSENT.includes(f)).map((f) => `UNRECOGNISED ${f}=${absent[f]}`)`, then joins declared-then-extra. That is the same body as the exported `latencyAbsentLine` at `scripts/agent/eval/adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1200-1205` (only difference: the helper's `absent ?? {}` normalisation, which the caller open-codes at line 991). The adapter's docblock at coderabbit.mjs:1186-1199 states the function is exported precisely so the wording is shared with `cost-latency.mjs` ("the wording matches so the two reports read alike") and so the unrecognised-row behaviour and declared-order rule live in one place; `docs/tasks/active/20260812-coderabbit-latency-todo.md:134-139` records the same rationale for extracting it in review. The reuse is trivially available: cost-latency.mjs:83 already imports from that exact module (`LATENCY_ABSENT, PUSH_PROXY_INTERVAL, SELF_TIMED_INTERVAL, TRIGGERS, corpusRecords, latencyCensus`) and the helper is unit-pinned at coderabbit.test.mjs:1240-1251, so the copy is untested and free to drift. This is a documented duplication/reuse violation, squarely in the design-fit lane and rated major by the rubric ("duplicates an existing module"). No guard or scope argument removes it.
